history: Found as a three-way split: Python and Rust refused at the decoder, the npm CLI and the verify page both substituted U+FFFD and verified the result. The npm half is closed. The browser half is OPEN.
note: A single 0xFF inside a string value. Python's CLI reads the file with path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') and raises UnicodeDecodeError before load_receipt is ever called; the Rust CLI reports 'cannot read: stream did not contain valid UTF-8' and exits non-zero; the npm parser now refuses with 'receipt is not valid UTF-8'. The verify page still substitutes U+FFFD and loads the document. The split is one level ABOVE every limit any of them check: it is in the decoder, not the parser. See 009 for why that is worse than it sounds.
